summary: Frontend-only verification of Telegram X compatibility fix via shared helper `/app/frontend/src/utils/telegram.ts`. Verified web fallback behavior for both `openTelegram` (contact detail) and `sendTelegramMessage` (group bulk send). On web, `Linking.canOpenURL('tg://...')` is not evaluated (Platform.OS==='web') so the helper directly calls `Linking.openURL('https://t.me/...')` which resolves to `window.open` -> confirmed captured URL is `https://t.me/durov` for the contact button and `https://t.me/durov?text=Hi%20TelTest!` for the bulk sender (with `{nome}` template substitution). No pageerrors on login, home, contact detail, or group screens. Native `tg://resolve?domain=...` cannot be exercised via web preview (requires physical device / native build), but the helper implementation is correct: it awaits `Linking.canOpenURL(nativeUri)` first on iOS/Android and falls back to the https URL only when the native scheme is not registered — this is precisely the pattern that unblocks Telegram X (Telegram X registers the same `tg://` scheme as stock Telegram, so `canOpenURL` returns true on either app).
critical_code_review_comments: src/utils/telegram.ts: `sendTelegramMessage` builds `tg://resolve?domain=<u>&text=<...>` — official Telegram deep-link docs do NOT document a `text` parameter on `tg://resolve` (only on `tg://msg_url`). It may be silently ignored on native, but functionally harmless (chat still opens). Consider using `tg://msg?to=<u>&text=...` or the documented `tg://msg_url?url=...&text=...` for stricter compliance. Fallback via https://t.me/<u>?text=... is honored by both clients when opened in-app.

src/utils/telegram.ts: `Linking.openURL('https://t.me/...')` on web navigates the current tab in some environments (React Native Web maps to `window.open` in newer versions). Tested here it triggers `window.open` — good — but note that if a browser blocks popups the fallback silently fails. Not a blocker for the fix.
seed_data_creation: Created + deleted TEST_TelTest contact and TEST_TGBulkGroup group via API within the test run (cleanup verified).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Telegram X fix verified on web. Native `tg://` path cannot be exercised in the web preview; only a physical device / TestFlight or Android APK can validate Telegram X actually opens. If user still reports Telegram X not opening on device, ask them to run `adb shell dumpsys package org.thunderdog.challegram` (Telegram X package) and verify the intent filter `tg` scheme is present, then re-check `Linking.canOpenURL` return value. The helper implementation is sound.
rca_of_issue: Original bug (only stock Telegram opened, not Telegram X): call sites were using `Linking.openURL('https://t.me/<u>')` directly. On Android, https URLs open the browser (or whichever browser handled the intent) instead of asking user which Telegram app to use. Fix: prefer `tg://resolve?domain=<u>` scheme first — both stock Telegram and Telegram X register this scheme, so Android's intent chooser will let the user pick either app. Fallback to https URL only when the native scheme is not registered (web / no client installed). Verified by test that on web the fallback URL is produced correctly.
